page: Amazon Web Services c6a.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 64-core AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at up to 3.6 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro Hypervisor, it delivers 128 dedicated virtual CPUs with simultaneous multithreading enabled across two threads per physical core. System memory totals 256 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached block storage and dedicated virtualization hardware. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 50 Gbps. Supported instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2.

Performance benchmark results show strong multi-threaded scaling and execution density. The instance achieves top-tier results in PassMark multi-core CPU testing, CPU encryption benchmarks, stress-ng multi-core load tests, and cached 16 KB read memory bandwidth. In application tests, Redis SET operations reach 137.19 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 55.53 GB/sec. Software compilation using Clang and Geekbench ray tracing performance both place in the upper performance tiers. Conversely, single-core benchmarks sit in the average tier, including single-threaded Geekbench scores, gzip compression, and LLM text generation rates for medium and large model sizes.

The hardware configuration yields high vCPU density per host socket, offering favorable qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out parallel compute jobs that do not require high memory-per-core ratios or ephemeral local storage. Because local disks are omitted, operational deployment relies entirely on EBS volumes over the 50 Gbps network link. The resource allocation profile makes the instance effective for multi-threaded batch processing, high-concurrency web serving fleets, software build pipelines, distributed database caching, and parallel scientific computations.
